patient.name: Linda Voss
patient.chiefComplaint: Severe low back pain after lifting grandchild, unable to ambulate

history.hpi: Patient was lifting her 2-year-old grandchild out of a crib this morning when she felt a sudden 'pop' and sharp pain in her lower back. Pain has progressively worsened over the past hour, now 9/10, sharp and band-like across the lumbar region without radiation into the legs. She is unable to stand upright or bear weight without severe pain and has been lying on the living room floor since the onset. Denies numbness, denies loss of bowel or bladder control, denies fever.
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee and toast, approximately 2 hours prior to onset
history.events: Daughter called 911 after finding patient unable to get up off the living room floor

scene.dispatch: 58-year-old female, back pain, unable to get up, residence
scene.location: Single-family home living room, patient supine on an area rug near a crib
scene.bystanders: Daughter present, witnessed onset while patient was lifting her grandchild out of the crib
visualCues: Patient lying supine and rigid, guarding her lower back
Grimacing and crying out with any attempted movement
No visible deformity, bruising, or swelling to the spine
Toddler being held by another family member nearby

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 58-year-old female supine on the floor, rigid with guarding, reporting severe lumbar back pain that began while lifting her grandchild. She is alert, oriented, and cooperative but in visible distress.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speaking full sentences between grimaces
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present and equal bilaterally, femoral pulses equal
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact and equal in both legs, sensation intact, no saddle anesthesia
otherFindings: Lumbar back pain 9/10, sharp and band-like, no radiation into legs
No pulsatile abdominal mass, no midline spinal step-off
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It hurts so bad, please don't make me move."

transitions.condition: Crew screens for life-threatening causes of back pain, assesses pain severity on a standard scale, and administers weight-based morphine per the Pain Management Guideline.

phases.name: Red flags screened, analgesia given
phases.description: Crew performs a focused assessment for life-threatening causes of back pain, positions the patient for comfort, and administers weight-based IV morphine for severe pain.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary survey confirms no airway, breathing, or circulation threats, the crew screens for red-flag causes of back pain (spinal cord compression, aortic dissection/AAA, pyelonephritis) and, finding none present, proceeds with analgesia for isolated musculoskeletal back pain.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and femoral pulses present and equal bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength and sensation intact and equal in both legs
otherFindings: Pain scale reassessed at 9/10 prior to medication
No costovertebral angle tenderness, no fever
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Please, can you give me something for the pain?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Screen for life-threatening back pain causes: neuro deficit, unequal femoral pulses, pulsatile mass, fever
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess for life-threatening causes of back pain, which may include: Spinal cord compression ... Aortic dissection or ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm ... Pyelonephritis
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out spinal cord compression, aortic emergency, and pyelonephritis before treating as isolated musculoskeletal pain.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess pain severity using the Numeric Rating Scale (patient is >12 years old)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Determine patient's pain score assessment using standard pain scale ... Greater than 12 years old: Self-report scale: Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a baseline pain score to guide dosing and measure response to treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Position patient for comfort while preparing IV access and medication
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Non-pharmacologic pain management options include Placement of the patient in a position of comfort
expectedActions.rationale: Reduces pain and anxiety while pharmacologic treatment is prepared.

expectedActions.shortAction: Morphine 7 mg IV (70 kg × 0.1 mg/kg = 7 mg; max initial dose 10 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For Moderate to Severe pain, analgesics include: Morphine sulfate: 0.1 mg/kg IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose is 10 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Weight-based opioid dosing for severe pain not attributable to a life-threatening cause.

transitions.condition: IV morphine is administered at the correct weight-based dose; pain score and vital signs improve over the following minutes.
Crew completes the red-flag screen but does not administer analgesia, or significantly delays medication administration, leaving the patient in severe uncontrolled pain.

phases.name: Morphine given, pain improves
phases.description: Following weight-based IV morphine, the patient's pain and vital signs improve. She is transported in a position of comfort with ongoing reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: After IV morphine 7 mg is administered, pain score and hemodynamics improve within several minutes; patient remains alert with stable respiratory status.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present and equal bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength and sensation intact and equal in both legs
otherFindings: Resting comfortably in position of comfort

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess pain score and vital signs after morphine; monitor respiratory status
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Pain severity scores should be recorded before and after analgesic medication administration and upon arrival at destination
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms treatment efficacy and screens for opioid-related respiratory depression.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport in position of comfort; reassess vitals and pain en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport in position of comfort and reassess as indicated
expectedActions.rationale: Continued reassessment ensures sustained pain control and early detection of adverse effects.

phases.name: Analgesia withheld despite severe pain
phases.description: Crew delays or withholds analgesia despite a completed red-flag screen showing isolated musculoskeletal back pain. The patient remains in severe pain, becoming increasingly distressed, tachycardic, and hypertensive.
phases.triggerCondition: Despite screening negative for red-flag causes, the crew does not administer weight-based morphine within a reasonable interval, leaving the patient's severe pain uncontrolled during scene time and transport.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and rapid
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength and sensation intact and equal in both legs
otherFindings: Pain remains 10/10, crying and unable to hold still
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Please, it still hurts so much, why won't it stop?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize uncontrolled pain; give morphine 7 mg IV now (70 kg × 0.1 mg/kg; max initial 10 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For Moderate to Severe pain, analgesics include: Morphine sulfate: 0.1 mg/kg IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose is 10 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Uncontrolled severe pain with worsening tachycardia and hypertension requires prompt correction of the delayed analgesia.
